newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook - China buying support wanes.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook - China buying support wanes.

text.p: Asian oil product prices are seen easing this week on more supplies and diminishing Chinese imports ahead of the Lunar New Year holidays, traders said on Monday.
"China's demand for both gas oil and fuel oil has already started to slow as most buyers have already stockpiled enough for the holiday season," said a trader.
The Chinese Lunar New Year holidays begin February 6 and could last up to 15 days. During the holidays, the market is expected to be quiet, Chinese traders said.
With weak demand in particular from China, fuel oil prices are expected to slip further as the market is already awash with supplies.
Traders said previous high fuel oil prices in Asia had opened the arbitrage window from the U.S. Gulf, prompting a western trader to bring a 40,000-tonne U.S. Gulf cargo to Asia.
They said Kuwait had also exported one more than its usual three spot 80,000-tonne cargoes of fuel oil to Singapore, dampening prices further.
Eyes would be on Taiwan's tender to buy 72,000 tonnes of February fuel oil which will close on January 15. Traders said Taiwan's tender could stem the slide in prices.
Fuel oil 180-centistoke was valued Friday at $119.00 per tonne, down from $124.00 a week earlier.

The gas oil market was also poised for more selling pressure this week as the market grapples with the prospect of higher supplies from South Korean, where crude processing capacity rose at least 600,000 barrels per day in 1996.
The large South Korean exports in December and January were easily absorbed by China, but for February Chinese demand is seen retreating due to the Lunar New Year holidays.
South Korea exported around 300,000 tonnes of spot cargoes in December with January exports estimated at around 250,000 tonnes, traders said.
China bought up to one million tonnes in December with January purchases also pegged at a similar level.
"The market is on edge as it sees how the new Korean product is absorbed," one trader said.
Already prices have slipped as more sellers emerged offering February cargoes. On Friday a late January 150,000-barrel cargo traded at $31.65 per barrel, free-on-board (fob) Singapore.
This compared with an intra-week high of $32.30 per barrel fob Singapore for a late January cargo.

Traders said hopes earlier last week of a larger Indian diesel purchase of up to 200,000-tonnes in its February supplementary tender were dashed over the weekend when Indian Oil Corp awarded a modest 135,000-tonnes.
India had already bought 720,000 tonnes of diesel in its first tender for February arrivals.

Further bearish news was on the cards, as Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) issued a tender to sell 225,000-250,000 barrels of 0.3 percent sulpfur diesel lifting January 26-February 15.
Traders said they are worried CPC might award more than its usual one or two cargoes, as it did last time, in the tender which closed on Monday.
CPC awarded three cargoes for December 11-20 lifting at $29.92 per barrel, free-on-board Kaoshiung in its last tender.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-870-3082)
